- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and model shows gradual upward drift, reduce forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast growth to 2–3% per period to avoid overbought bias.  
- If official event net supply is strongly bearish (e.g., > -15) and sentiment is negative, model underestimates downside — add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.  
- When sentiment is mixed (e.g., 0.33–0.67) and model is flat, introduce slight upward drift to reflect latent bullish sentiment.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if recent 18-day history shows strong downward trend, model often fails to capture mean reversion — adjust forecast to include 1–2% upward correction after 3–5 periods.  
- If official events are frequent and supply net is negative, model tends to overestimate price stability — reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.2 per event period.
